repayments.title: Revenue and settlements, not only spending
repayments.body: Add income — a deposit returned, a refund, a shared payout — and split it the same four ways, on a schedule if it repeats. Repayments are recorded as settlements, and the group's suggested payments are worked out for you.

useCases.title: If money keeps moving between the same few people, this is for you.
useCases.intro: Six situations people tend to arrive with. Each one leans on a different part of Balancia.

trip.title: Organising a trip with friends
trip.body: Flights booked months ago, a villa deposit one person fronted, dinners paid by whoever's card was closest, half of it in another currency. Add each cost as it happens and Balancia keeps every currency straight, then suggests the payments that clear the whole trip when you get home.

flat.title: Sharing a flat
flat.body: Rent, electricity, internet and the weekly shop, month after month. Set the repeating ones up once and they appear on schedule. When somebody moves out mid-month, an exact-amount split handles the awkward part.

partner.title: Living costs with a partner
partner.body: Two incomes that aren't the same size, and a fifty-fifty split that never felt right. Give the shared pot a percentage or a share ratio instead — 60/40, or three shares to two — and every expense follows it without a conversation each time.

event.title: A wedding, a stag do, a group gift
event.body: One or two people carry the big bookings while a dozen others owe a share. Guests join the group through a link, so nobody has to make an account for a single weekend — and when the venue returns the deposit, that comes back in as income and reduces what everyone owes.

ownership.title: Something you own together
ownership.body: A car between siblings, a boat between friends, a holiday house in the family. Insurance and maintenance recur; when you rent the place out, that revenue is recorded and split the same way the costs are. Receipts stay attached to the expense they belong to.

club.title: A club, a team, a band
club.body: Kit and pitch fees going out, subs and gig money coming in. Record both sides in one group, split payouts by shares when they aren't equal, and export the year as an Excel workbook for whoever keeps the books.

comparison.title: Bring the group with you.
comparison.body: Upload a Splitwise CSV export or JSON backup and Balancia shows you exactly what it will create before writing anything. Run the same file twice and nothing is duplicated. You do not have to start from an empty group.

selfHosting.title: Nobody sits between you and your money.
selfHosting.body: Balancia is free software under the AGPL-3.0-or-later licence. It runs from one Docker Compose file with PostgreSQL and a background worker, and requires no third-party services. Telemetry exists only to help improve the tool, is off by default on self-hosted instances, and never includes personal data or amounts.
selfHosting.bodyAnalytics: Balancia is free software under the AGPL-3.0-or-later licence. It runs from one Docker Compose file with PostgreSQL and a background worker, and requires no third-party services. Telemetry never includes personal data or amounts. On this instance, an administrator has enabled anonymous counts for the public landing and sign-in screens; no page inside the application is counted.
selfHosting.exportBody: Leaving is as easy as arriving: every group exports to CSV, Excel or JSON from its settings, and a self-hosted instance keeps its database and receipts on disks you own.

selfHosting.licenseNote: The AGPL adds one obligation: run a modified version as a network service and you must offer its users the source. That protects the people trusting your instance with their financial history.

status.title: Young software, kept honest.
status.body: Everything on this page exists in the repository today. What is finished, what is partial and what has not been started is written down rather than implied — including the parts that are not built yet.

free.question: Is it actually free?
free.answer: Yes. An account on this instance costs nothing and no feature is held back. The software itself is free under AGPL-3.0-or-later, so you can also run your own copy and never depend on this one.

accounts.question: Do the people I split with need an account?
accounts.answer: No. Invite them through a revocable link. Guests can view the group, add and edit expenses, settle up and upload receipts, but never manage people, links or the group itself.

sharing.question: How do I split an expense between several people?
sharing.answer: Add the amount, choose who paid and select the people included. You can split the expense equally, enter exact amounts, assign percentages or use custom shares. Balances update automatically.

unequal.question: Can I split an expense unequally?
unequal.answer: Yes. Enter the exact amount for each person, assign percentages or use weighted shares, such as three shares for one person and two for another. Balancia always keeps the total exact.

export.question: Can I get my data back out?
export.answer: Any group downloads as JSON — the complete record, amounts exactly as stored — or as CSV or an Excel workbook, from its settings page.

currency.question: What happens with different currencies?
currency.answer: Keep each currency balanced on its own, or convert into one base currency at a rate frozen when the expense is recorded, so historical expenses are never silently recalculated. Daily rates can be filled in from the European Central Bank's published figures; that is off by default.

privacy.question: Is anything about my spending sent anywhere?
privacy.answer: No. Telemetry never carries personal data or amounts — it exists only to help improve the tool, and on a self-hosted instance it is off by default. Even the category guessing runs locally, with no AI service involved. Optional integrations only make network requests when an administrator enables them.

splitwise.question: Can I import my data from Splitwise?
splitwise.answer: Yes. Balancia accepts a Splitwise group CSV export or JSON backup. It previews the import before bringing in expenses, settlements, currencies and people. Final shares are preserved as exact amounts, but the original split-method label and historical exchange rates are not recreated.

openSource.question: Is Balancia open source?
openSource.answer: Yes. Balancia's source code is public at github.com/sebitr/balancia under the AGPL-3.0-or-later licence, where the community can inspect, audit and improve it.

selfHost.question: How hard is it to run myself?
selfHost.answer: Three commands: clone the repository, run the bootstrap script, then bring it up with Docker Compose. PostgreSQL, migrations, the app and its worker all start together. Reverse-proxy examples for Caddy, Traefik and nginx are in the docs.

devices.question: Does Balancia work on iPhone and Android?
devices.answer: Yes. Balancia works in a modern browser on desktop, iPhone, iPad and Android. You can also add the progressive web app to your home screen so that it opens like a regular app. It is not distributed through the App Store or Play Store.

comparison.question: How is Balancia different from Splitwise and Tricount?
comparison.answer: Balancia is an open-source, self-hostable alternative to Splitwise and Tricount. Its differences include guest participation without an account, progressive web app installation, four split methods, multi-currency groups and Splitwise data import. Features and offers from each service may change.

seo.description: Balancia is free, open-source software for splitting shared expenses in a group. It handles equal, exact, percentage and share-based splits, several payers on one bill, multiple currencies, recurring expenses, income and settlements. It can be used on a hosted instance with a free account, or self-hosted on your own server under the AGPL-3.0-or-later licence.
